Найновіший зі списку китайських хмарочосів-рекордсменів - пекінська #CiticTower
528-метрова гігантеса зі сталі і скла змінила столичний скайлайн у 2018-му. 
Її лаконічні обриси, натхненні церемоніальною вазою для вина "цзунь", надовго залишаться домінантою у ландшафті Пекіну.
Ііііі швидко вилетять із світової десятки😉 

Нинішній державний циркуляр у сфері містобудування обмежує "зріст" нових хмарочосів відміткою у 500 метрів. І, що важливіше, закликає відмовитись від "дивакуватих, ксеноцентричних форм та бездумних запозичень" на користь екологічної забудови та архітектурної самобутності... Здається, Китай вже награвся у копіпаст☺️ І хоча мені подобаються результати останніх десятиліть, коли мегаполіси КНР були плацдармом для виру ідей іноземних архітекторів, я вже у передчутті "нової старої" далекосхідної естетики🎎🌇

...а Citic Tower буде особливою для мене безвідносно рейтингів. Її срібні відблиски ми спостерігали щоранку із вікна нашої пекінської кухні🤗
Що показує вам ваше вікно, друзі?

Чего только не сделаешь, чтобы оказаться в рейтинге самых высоких зданий планеты! Первоначальный проект башен Greenland Central Plaza в китайском городе Наньчан «подрос» на 14 метров, чтобы попасть в список трёхсотметровых строений - их высота составила 303 метра. Но из-за этого нагрузка на основание сильно увеличивалась, и поэтому архитекторам пришлось пойти на хитрость - установить в верхней части небоскрёба конструкцию из поворачивающихся стеклянных жалюзи, чтобы сквозь отверстия беспрепятственно проходил ветер. Но интересны и сами стёкла! У основания здание квадратное в плане, но чем выше оно становится, тем более закруглённым становится фасад. Чтобы добиться такого эффекта, строители использовали панели, созданные при помощи технологии «холодного сгибания», благодаря чему можно добиться любой формы оконного стекла.

Tianfu Square, Chengdu, Sichuan Province (Part 2)

Tianfu Square is the busiest area in the commercial and business district of the city. 

Paved with light coloured granite and lined with trees and flowers and water features, the square is an open leisure place for people to have a rest and appreciate the modern development of Chengdu. 

The structures and open space is just fascinating. I took my time here to enjoy the hustle and bustle of urban China. 

I know that I didn't have enough time in Chengdu, as there was so much I wanted to do, but couldn't. I knew already I was going to leave a little regretful.

A #skyscraper in #guiyang , #china , has attracted headlines thanks to a daring water feature built into its facade. On one side, the 121-meter (397-foot) tall Liebian Building in Guiyang, China, features a spectacular waterfall, providing a dramatic spectacle from the plaza below. At 108-meters (350-feet), the waterfall is among the tallest artificial waterfalls in the world—and easily the largest artificial waterfall located in an urban area, with other record breakers being artificial additions to river and canal networks, "Follow @arc.insprd for architectural inspiration.

Найновіший зі списку китайських хмарочосів-рекордсменів - пекінська #CiticTower
528-метрова гігантеса зі сталі і скла змінила столичний скайлайн у 2018-му. 
Її лаконічні обриси, натхненні церемоніальною вазою для вина "цзунь", надовго залишаться домінантою у ландшафті Пекіну.
Ііііі швидко вилетять із світової десятки😉 

Нинішній державний циркуляр у сфері містобудування обмежує "зріст" нових хмарочосів відміткою у 500 метрів. І, що важливіше, закликає відмовитись від "дивакуватих, ксеноцентричних форм та бездумних запозичень" на користь екологічної забудови та архітектурної самобутності... Здається, Китай вже награвся у копіпаст☺️ І хоча мені подобаються результати останніх десятиліть, коли мегаполіси КНР були плацдармом для виру ідей іноземних архітекторів, я вже у передчутті "нової старої" далекосхідної естетики🎎🌇

...а Citic Tower буде особливою для мене безвідносно рейтингів. Її срібні відблиски ми спостерігали щоранку із вікна нашої пекінської кухні🤗
Що показує вам ваше вікно, друзі?

Но из-за этого нагрузка на основание сильно увеличивалась, и поэтому архитекторам пришлось пойти на хитрость - установить в верхней части небоскрёба конструкцию из поворачивающихся стеклянных жалюзи, чтобы сквозь отверстия беспрепятственно проходил ветер. Но интересны и сами стёкла! У основания здание квадратное в плане, но чем выше оно становится, тем более закруглённым становится фасад. Чтобы добиться такого эффекта, строители использовали панели, созданные при помощи технологии «холодного сгибания», благодаря чему можно добиться любой формы оконного стекла.

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

Seeds are the main raw material used to make Chinese liquor. At the entrance lobby, various seeds are placed in Plexiglas tubes to create a vibrant screen with a huge pattern.

The original house is preserved, and does not destabilize the rest of the adjoining housing. The house is based on a modular architecture, this is possible by the use of prefabricated materials. This off -site production allows a quick realization once on site, which turns out to be very cheap.The house itself is completely adapted to its inhabitants and personalized to their uses. This is an essential notion in the development of DTP projects: the human being is at the heart. In the Huang house, on a poor area of 15m2, the kitchen and water space on the ground floor, followed by the bedroom on the first  floor. This minimal relationship to space projects the need for sharing and common spaces towards the outside and thus an appropriation of the street. For the Fang house, small front and back outdoor spaces are  created on the plot, the 25m2 house proposes a 1 bedroom housing on one level.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

Shuifa Geographic Information Industrial Park Exhibition Center 
#Jinan, #China

The project is located in the Changqing Economic Development Zone, 20 kilometers away from the city centre of Jinan. In order to give visitors the best viewing experience, the designer has isolated the area from the surrounding environment and has created a relatively enclosed space.

The building’s main functions are hosting residential sales expos, property expos, and offices. The main entrance is located on the west side. In order to eliminate the visual impact of the messy surrounding environment, geometrical hills are designed to surround the square, which slowly rises as people enter the site, gradually blocking out the view. Mountains, water, and marble are fused together in this undeveloped wilderness.

A second layer is set outside the main structure - perforated plating, so that the building is enveloped within the perforated plating, forming a relatively enclosed space. The curtain wall sections are slanted, nestled, and interlaced inside, and the gap between the sections naturally forms the entrance of the building. Everything happens inside the space covered by the perforated plate curtain wall, connected to the outside world only through the irregular gaps. The interior of the building is obscured by the white perforated plating, and as night falls, light shines through the perforated plates to make the whole building glow, like a piece of shiny marble standing in the wilderness.

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

"Jiu Qu", a brick shaped solid composite of yeast and mold, is used for saccharification and fermentation. We used these vegetal bricks to create the counter of the bar, which gives an olfactive experience to the user. The countertop is made of custom terrazzo fabricated on site with pieces of green glass from local bottles of liquor.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Laura Chambefort Master 1 ENSA Versailles(…)The setting up of a plugin house in the heart of the historical district allowed to link at the same time a cheap dwelling in a lively and solidary district and in the center. According to PAO, the cost of living in a plugin house would be «thirty  mes lower than the cost of buying a classic apartment».However these districts having been disinvested since decades by the governmental services, the water networks, but especially of sewers are not present. Thus within the house it was necessary to adapt to the site in order to make the house the most comfortable to its inhabitants. PAO has thus realized the house through the technical constraints, sanitary (toilets out of water), relation to the light (double heights and bays on the roofs), but also through the neighborhood to keep their atomospheric living conditions (light & ventilation). In the axonometry below, the house by the modularity of its structure was entirely thought by its inclusiveness with the neighbors, that it is in the phase of drawing but also during its realization.The plugin house by these various aspects thus allows a renewal of the fabric of the Hutong. By using prefabricated and light materials, it is adapted to the demand for housing in a real estate market without limits. And it  fits perfectly into a way of life open to the outside world and close to the historical idea of the Hutong. These projects revitalize and infuse new models of conscious density into the urban fabric of Beijing.The interview is especially based on the analysis of 2 plugin houses:Shenzen's Shangwei Village, province du Guangdong South China, 2018Mrs Fan's house Historic Beijing Hutong, 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #pao #peoplearchitectureoffice #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #prefabricated #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history

I learned from @colleudumond (merci!) that the garden I shared yesterday at Chaumont-sur-Loire was designed by Wang Shu, a Chinese architect who has won the Pritzker prize. I looked up more of his work and was very interested in much of what I saw and read. Both in terms of how he and several other architects have been changing Chinese architecture in the last 20 or so years, but also in the specifics of how. Particularly interesting to me was Wang Shu’s Ningbo History Museum where he used materials salvaged from building and villages that had been cleared for the project in the facade. In his own words the design was a kind of resistance against the thoughtfulness destruction of their history. This was designed in 2008 around the same time as the Beijing Olympics, so I can only imagine how relevant that statement was.

Interesting to me is that I recognize a global trend that we also saw in Europe and elsewhere in the same period using salvaged and traditional materials in a way that honored but also transcends the vernacular.

The museum intentionally reminds us of both large ruins and fortresses and is an imposing figure in the landscape. The angles of the facade create tension and different scale spaces from very large to intimate, and paths seem to zigzag between. The contrast of the deeply textural and detailed facade to the enormous scale of the building adds so much. It is the materials that bring the whole building to life for me and make it most interesting.

In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

"Jiu Qu", a brick shaped solid composite of yeast and mold, is used for saccharification and fermentation. We used these vegetal bricks to create the counter of the bar, which gives an olfactive experience to the user. The countertop is made of custom terrazzo fabricated on site with pieces of green glass from local bottles of liquor.

Shuifa Geographic Information Industrial Park Exhibition Center 
#Jinan, #China

The project is located in the Changqing Economic Development Zone, 20 kilometers away from the city centre of Jinan. In order to give visitors the best viewing experience, the designer has isolated the area from the surrounding environment and has created a relatively enclosed space.

The building’s main functions are hosting residential sales expos, property expos, and offices. The main entrance is located on the west side. In order to eliminate the visual impact of the messy surrounding environment, geometrical hills are designed to surround the square, which slowly rises as people enter the site, gradually blocking out the view. Mountains, water, and marble are fused together in this undeveloped wilderness.

A second layer is set outside the main structure - perforated plating, so that the building is enveloped within the perforated plating, forming a relatively enclosed space. The curtain wall sections are slanted, nestled, and interlaced inside, and the gap between the sections naturally forms the entrance of the building. Everything happens inside the space covered by the perforated plate curtain wall, connected to the outside world only through the irregular gaps. The interior of the building is obscured by the white perforated plating, and as night falls, light shines through the perforated plates to make the whole building glow, like a piece of shiny marble standing in the wilderness.

I learned from @colleudumond (merci!) that the garden I shared yesterday at Chaumont-sur-Loire was designed by Wang Shu, a Chinese architect who has won the Pritzker prize. I looked up more of his work and was very interested in much of what I saw and read. Both in terms of how he and several other architects have been changing Chinese architecture in the last 20 or so years, but also in the specifics of how. Particularly interesting to me was Wang Shu’s Ningbo History Museum where he used materials salvaged from building and villages that had been cleared for the project in the facade. In his own words the design was a kind of resistance against the thoughtfulness destruction of their history. This was designed in 2008 around the same time as the Beijing Olympics, so I can only imagine how relevant that statement was.

Interesting to me is that I recognize a global trend that we also saw in Europe and elsewhere in the same period using salvaged and traditional materials in a way that honored but also transcends the vernacular.

The museum intentionally reminds us of both large ruins and fortresses and is an imposing figure in the landscape. The angles of the facade create tension and different scale spaces from very large to intimate, and paths seem to zigzag between. The contrast of the deeply textural and detailed facade to the enormous scale of the building adds so much. It is the materials that bring the whole building to life for me and make it most interesting.

In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

"Jiu Qu", a brick shaped solid composite of yeast and mold, is used for saccharification and fermentation. We used these vegetal bricks to create the counter of the bar, which gives an olfactive experience to the user. The countertop is made of custom terrazzo fabricated on site with pieces of green glass from local bottles of liquor.

#Jinan, #China

The project is located in the Changqing Economic Development Zone, 20 kilometers away from the city centre of Jinan. In order to give visitors the best viewing experience, the designer has isolated the area from the surrounding environment and has created a relatively enclosed space.

The building’s main functions are hosting residential sales expos, property expos, and offices. The main entrance is located on the west side. In order to eliminate the visual impact of the messy surrounding environment, geometrical hills are designed to surround the square, which slowly rises as people enter the site, gradually blocking out the view. Mountains, water, and marble are fused together in this undeveloped wilderness.

A second layer is set outside the main structure - perforated plating, so that the building is enveloped within the perforated plating, forming a relatively enclosed space. The curtain wall sections are slanted, nestled, and interlaced inside, and the gap between the sections naturally forms the entrance of the building. Everything happens inside the space covered by the perforated plate curtain wall, connected to the outside world only through the irregular gaps. The interior of the building is obscured by the white perforated plating, and as night falls, light shines through the perforated plates to make the whole building glow, like a piece of shiny marble standing in the wilderness.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Marine Fritsch Master 1 @ensa_versailles The project of No. 28 Dayuan Hu Tong, titled «Miniature Beijing», is a transformation project by Atelier Li Xinggang completed in 2017 and located in the Old City district of Beijing. Initially, the original building was a 262 square meter common courtyard house. It has been transformed into five apartments with independent courtyards, as well as a space accessible to public that hosts a cafe and tea house. This project combines old urban renewal, courtyard renovation and a research on ideal house. Indeed, the layout of the «garden house» and the «public unit»  fits into the structure of contemporary society, transforming the courtyard house into a «miniature community.» The design of the apartments in minimal size serves the spiritual construction of the «garden house harmonization», and transforms the experience of everyday poetry and urban landscape into the «ideal living environment» through the narrative of space. This project also provides an extension of public space from the street and completes the established «street + residential unit» model, transforming the courtyard into a «miniature community». This collective space can be used and shared by all residents of the unit on a daily basis, and can be opened to neighbouring hutongs and foreign visitors. This space then becomes a place of public service shared by a larger number of neighbors and reinforces its «community» character.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the ‘Miniature Beijing’ project : a conversion of No. 28 Dayuan Hutong Beijing in collective housing, sharing spaces and facilities

With their experience after setting up their office in the heart of the Hutong of Beijing. The agency questions the possible rehabilitation of historical districts of the Chinese capital.The Hutong are the historical urban system of Beijing, characterized by the tangle of alleys and courtyards, the buildings are arranged in a  fine and very dense mesh.Some of them are more than 700 years old, and the population of these historic districts was abandoned by their inhabitants who preferred to move to the Beijing suburbs with more modern housing. Thus the Hutong, the historical heart of the capital, became a slum. It is in this context that Mrs Fan, the inhabitant of the plugin house realized by PAO, grew up. When she was young, her parents originally from Hutong chose to move to the suburbs. Mrs. Fan, once married and an adult, decided to become independent. PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Marine Fritsch Master 1 @ensa_versailles The project of No. 28 Dayuan Hu Tong, titled «Miniature Beijing», is a transformation project by Atelier Li Xinggang completed in 2017 and located in the Old City district of Beijing. Initially, the original building was a 262 square meter common courtyard house. It has been transformed into five apartments with independent courtyards, as well as a space accessible to public that hosts a cafe and tea house. This project combines old urban renewal, courtyard renovation and a research on ideal house. Indeed, the layout of the «garden house» and the «public unit»  fits into the structure of contemporary society, transforming the courtyard house into a «miniature community.» The design of the apartments in minimal size serves the spiritual construction of the «garden house harmonization», and transforms the experience of everyday poetry and urban landscape into the «ideal living environment» through the narrative of space. This project also provides an extension of public space from the street and completes the established «street + residential unit» model, transforming the courtyard into a «miniature community». This collective space can be used and shared by all residents of the unit on a daily basis, and can be opened to neighbouring hutongs and foreign visitors. This space then becomes a place of public service shared by a larger number of neighbors and reinforces its «community» character.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the ‘Miniature Beijing’ project : a conversion of No. 28 Dayuan Hutong Beijing in collective housing, sharing spaces and facilities#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #cag #atelierli #lixinggang #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #lifestyle #collectivehousing #minimalliving #insideoutside #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history

As a traditional water-town with a rich cultural heritage, Doumen faces challenges in balancing preservation with modern development while striving to boost its tourism industry. The rendering above showcases one of the many small designs under our overall design strategy, where we propose integrating the traditional craft of celadon—an intangible cultural heritage—into the space, creating a seamless blend of local craftsmanship and contemporary design. PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Laura Chambefort Master 1 ENSA Versailles(…)The setting up of a plugin house in the heart of the historical district allowed to link at the same time a cheap dwelling in a lively and solidary district and in the center. According to PAO, the cost of living in a plugin house would be «thirty  mes lower than the cost of buying a classic apartment».However these districts having been disinvested since decades by the governmental services, the water networks, but especially of sewers are not present. Thus within the house it was necessary to adapt to the site in order to make the house the most comfortable to its inhabitants. PAO has thus realized the house through the technical constraints, sanitary (toilets out of water), relation to the light (double heights and bays on the roofs), but also through the neighborhood to keep their atomospheric living conditions (light & ventilation). In the axonometry below, the house by the modularity of its structure was entirely thought by its inclusiveness with the neighbors, that it is in the phase of drawing but also during its realization.The plugin house by these various aspects thus allows a renewal of the fabric of the Hutong. By using prefabricated and light materials, it is adapted to the demand for housing in a real estate market without limits. And it  fits perfectly into a way of life open to the outside world and close to the historical idea of the Hutong. These projects revitalize and infuse new models of conscious density into the urban fabric of Beijing.The interview is especially based on the analysis of 2 plugin houses:Shenzen's Shangwei Village, province du Guangdong South China, 2018Mrs Fan's house Historic Beijing Hutong, 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #pao #peoplearchitectureoffice #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #prefabricated #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Marine Fritsch Master 1 @ensa_versailles The project of No. 28 Dayuan Hu Tong, titled «Miniature Beijing», is a transformation project by Atelier Li Xinggang completed in 2017 and located in the Old City district of Beijing. Initially, the original building was a 262 square meter common courtyard house. It has been transformed into five apartments with independent courtyards, as well as a space accessible to public that hosts a cafe and tea house. This project combines old urban renewal, courtyard renovation and a research on ideal house. Indeed, the layout of the «garden house» and the «public unit»  fits into the structure of contemporary society, transforming the courtyard house into a «miniature community.» The design of the apartments in minimal size serves the spiritual construction of the «garden house harmonization», and transforms the experience of everyday poetry and urban landscape into the «ideal living environment» through the narrative of space. This project also provides an extension of public space from the street and completes the established «street + residential unit» model, transforming the courtyard into a «miniature community». This collective space can be used and shared by all residents of the unit on a daily basis, and can be opened to neighbouring hutongs and foreign visitors. This space then becomes a place of public service shared by a larger number of neighbors and reinforces its «community» character.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the ‘Miniature Beijing’ project : a conversion of No. 28 Dayuan Hutong Beijing in collective housing, sharing spaces and facilities#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #cag #atelierli #lixinggang #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #lifestyle #collectivehousing #minimalliving #insideoutside #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project (with my partners of @zhijian_workshop) :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

"Jiu Qu", a brick shaped solid composite of yeast and mold, is used for saccharification and fermentation. We used these vegetal bricks to create the counter of the bar, which gives an olfactive experience to the user. The countertop is made of custom terrazzo fabricated on site with pieces of green glass from local bottles of liquor.

The village of Shangwei, was abandoned in parallel with the strong expansion of the adjacent city Shenzen. This one has swallowed the faces near leaving no time to those to be able to integrate into the city, the inhabitants of these villages preferring to migrate to more modern housing. The result is the appearance of several ruined villages in the heart of Shenzen, in the middle of a very high urban density.The project is therefore installed in this particular context. The city having for project to rehabilitate these vacant spaces, the question arises of a form of dwelling linking the centenary architectures and light salubrious forms of dwelling and linked to intrasement to its inhabitant. He is the founder of Run atelier dedicated to 3 domains : general projects, teaching and the last one is focusing on «reshaping the value of places». One of his goals is to lead the traditional Chinese archi- tecture in a contemporary way. Within his teaching career he founded the Construction Society, an academic group that focused on residential wood architecture and craftsmanship. For him as an architect : exploring and researching materials are fundamentals.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Laura Chambefort @laura_cbf Master 1 ENSA Versailles @ensa_versailles (…) Thus PAO @peoplesarchitecture proposes a white prefabricated structure wrapped by an abandoned house left in ruins. The original house is preserved, and does not destabilize the rest of the adjoining housing. The house is based on a modular architecture, this is possible by the use of prefabricated materials. This off -site production allows a quick realization once on site, which turns out to be very cheap.The house itself is completely adapted to its inhabitants and personalized to their uses. This is an essential notion in the development of DTP projects: the human being is at the heart. In the Huang house, on a poor area of 15m2, the kitchen and water space on the ground floor, followed by the bedroom on the first  floor. This minimal relationship to space projects the need for sharing and common spaces towards the outside and thus an appropriation of the street. For the Fang house, small front and back outdoor spaces are  created on the plot, the 25m2 house proposes a 1 bedroom housing on one level.

Pictures @peoplesarchitecture : Huang’s houseThe interview is especially based on the analysis of 2 plugin houses:Shenzen's Shangwei Village, province du Guangdong South China, 2018Mrs Fan's house Historic Beijing Hutong, 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #pao #peoplearchitectureoffice #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #prefabricated #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history #minimalliving #lightweightarchitecture #prefabricated #prefabricatedhouse

Shuifa Geographic Information Industrial Park Exhibition Center 
#Jinan, #China

The project is located in the Changqing Economic Development Zone, 20 kilometers away from the city centre of Jinan. In order to give visitors the best viewing experience, the designer has isolated the area from the surrounding environment and has created a relatively enclosed space.

The building’s main functions are hosting residential sales expos, property expos, and offices. The main entrance is located on the west side. In order to eliminate the visual impact of the messy surrounding environment, geometrical hills are designed to surround the square, which slowly rises as people enter the site, gradually blocking out the view. Mountains, water, and marble are fused together in this undeveloped wilderness.

A second layer is set outside the main structure - perforated plating, so that the building is enveloped within the perforated plating, forming a relatively enclosed space. The curtain wall sections are slanted, nestled, and interlaced inside, and the gap between the sections naturally forms the entrance of the building. Everything happens inside the space covered by the perforated plate curtain wall, connected to the outside world only through the irregular gaps. The interior of the building is obscured by the white perforated plating, and as night falls, light shines through the perforated plates to make the whole building glow, like a piece of shiny marble standing in the wilderness.

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

Seeds are the main raw material used to make Chinese liquor. We directly integrated seeds in the paint of the walls to create a unique texture.

The original house is preserved, and does not destabilize the rest of the adjoining housing. The house is based on a modular architecture, this is possible by the use of prefabricated materials. This off -site production allows a quick realization once on site, which turns out to be very cheap.The house itself is completely adapted to its inhabitants and personalized to their uses. This is an essential notion in the development of DTP projects: the human being is at the heart. In the Huang house, on a poor area of 15m2, the kitchen and water space on the ground floor, followed by the bedroom on the first  floor. This minimal relationship to space projects the need for sharing and common spaces towards the outside and thus an appropriation of the street. For the Fang house, small front and back outdoor spaces are  created on the plot, the 25m2 house proposes a 1 bedroom housing on one level.

Pictures @peoplesarchitecture : Huang’s houseThe interview is especially based on the analysis of 2 plugin houses:Shenzen's Shangwei Village, province du Guangdong South China, 2018Mrs Fan's house Historic Beijing Hutong, 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #pao #peoplearchitectureoffice #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #prefabricated #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history #minimalliving #lightweightarchitecture #prefabricated #prefabricatedhouse

In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

They wanted to have modular typologies to combine them in different ways and create new areas in the village, to create unique space into a modern pattern of living. They set the buildings to create space between them, with differents uses for each of them. Through the collaborative sessions with the inhabitants, they were able to propose differents uses for the types of outdoor spaces: relaxing, nature connection or storage for instance. The distance between the buildings allows public spaces. The urban fabric match perfectly with the surrounding land: mountains and water, a very traditional chinese landscape. Their work on the roofs really have an impact on the insertion of the village into its landscape.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Dongziguan village affordable Housing 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #lineplus #mengfanhao #architectureinterviews #lifestyle #collectivehousing #insideoutside #landscape #waterscape #publicspace #commons #collaborativearchitecture #context #history #materiality

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

"Jiu Qu", a brick shaped solid composite of yeast and mold, is used for saccharification and fermentation. We used these vegetal bricks to create the counter of the bar, which gives an olfactive experience to the user. The countertop is made of custom terrazzo fabricated on site with pieces of green glass from local bottles of liquor.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Laura Chambefort Master 1 ENSA Versailles(…)The setting up of a plugin house in the heart of the historical district allowed to link at the same time a cheap dwelling in a lively and solidary district and in the center. According to PAO, the cost of living in a plugin house would be «thirty  mes lower than the cost of buying a classic apartment».However these districts having been disinvested since decades by the governmental services, the water networks, but especially of sewers are not present. Thus within the house it was necessary to adapt to the site in order to make the house the most comfortable to its inhabitants. PAO has thus realized the house through the technical constraints, sanitary (toilets out of water), relation to the light (double heights and bays on the roofs), but also through the neighborhood to keep their atomospheric living conditions (light & ventilation). In the axonometry below, the house by the modularity of its structure was entirely thought by its inclusiveness with the neighbors, that it is in the phase of drawing but also during its realization.The plugin house by these various aspects thus allows a renewal of the fabric of the Hutong. By using prefabricated and light materials, it is adapted to the demand for housing in a real estate market without limits. And it  fits perfectly into a way of life open to the outside world and close to the historical idea of the Hutong. These projects revitalize and infuse new models of conscious density into the urban fabric of Beijing.The interview is especially based on the analysis of 2 plugin houses:Shenzen's Shangwei Village, province du Guangdong South China, 2018Mrs Fan's house Historic Beijing Hutong, 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #pao #peoplearchitectureoffice #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #prefabricated #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history

The result is the appearance of several ruined villages in the heart of Shenzen, in the middle of a very high urban density.The project is therefore installed in this particular context. The city having for project to rehabilitate these vacant spaces, the question arises of a form of dwelling linking the centenary architectures and light salubrious forms of dwelling and linked to intrasement to its inhabitant. Shuifa Geographic Information Industrial Park Exhibition Center 
#Jinan, #China

The project is located in the Changqing Economic Development Zone, 20 kilometers away from the city centre of Jinan. In order to give visitors the best viewing experience, the designer has isolated the area from the surrounding environment and has created a relatively enclosed space.

The building’s main functions are hosting residential sales expos, property expos, and offices. The main entrance is located on the west side. In order to eliminate the visual impact of the messy surrounding environment, geometrical hills are designed to surround the square, which slowly rises as people enter the site, gradually blocking out the view. Mountains, water, and marble are fused together in this undeveloped wilderness.

A second layer is set outside the main structure - perforated plating, so that the building is enveloped within the perforated plating, forming a relatively enclosed space. The curtain wall sections are slanted, nestled, and interlaced inside, and the gap between the sections naturally forms the entrance of the building. Everything happens inside the space covered by the perforated plate curtain wall, connected to the outside world only through the irregular gaps. The interior of the building is obscured by the white perforated plating, and as night falls, light shines through the perforated plates to make the whole building glow, like a piece of shiny marble standing in the wilderness.

They wanted to have modular typologies to combine them in different ways and create new areas in the village, to create unique space into a modern pattern of living. They set the buildings to create space between them, with differents uses for each of them. Through the collaborative sessions with the inhabitants, they were able to propose differents uses for the types of outdoor spaces: relaxing, nature connection or storage for instance. The distance between the buildings allows public spaces. The urban fabric match perfectly with the surrounding land: mountains and water, a very traditional chinese landscape. Their work on the roofs really have an impact on the insertion of the village into its landscape.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Dongziguan village affordable Housing 2016#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #lineplus #mengfanhao #architectureinterviews #lifestyle #collectivehousing #insideoutside #landscape #waterscape #publicspace #commons #collaborativearchitecture #context #history #materiality

Rehabilitación de Cantina de Mineros - Aurelien Chen Architecture - China

La restauración de este patrimonio industrial es una sutil reinterpretación de la “Era Roja” de China. Este edificio de los años 70 solía ser el comedor de los trabajadores de las minas de carbón. Se encuentra junto a lo que solían ser los edificios de oficinas de la mina de carbón, que fueron construidos en 1912 por arquitectos alemanes, y presenta las características típicas de la arquitectura occidental en China de la época, con un uso intensivo de elementos de arco.

The village of Shangwei, was abandoned in parallel with the strong expansion of the adjacent city Shenzen. This one has swallowed the faces near leaving no time to those to be able to integrate into the city, the inhabitants of these villages preferring to migrate to more modern housing. The result is the appearance of several ruined villages in the heart of Shenzen, in the middle of a very high urban density.The project is therefore installed in this particular context. The city having for project to rehabilitate these vacant spaces, the question arises of a form of dwelling linking the centenary architectures and light salubrious forms of dwelling and linked to intrasement to its inhabitant. In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : Marine Fritsch Master 1 @ensa_versailles The project of No. 28 Dayuan Hu Tong, titled «Miniature Beijing», is a transformation project by Atelier Li Xinggang completed in 2017 and located in the Old City district of Beijing. Initially, the original building was a 262 square meter common courtyard house. It has been transformed into five apartments with independent courtyards, as well as a space accessible to public that hosts a cafe and tea house. This project combines old urban renewal, courtyard renovation and a research on ideal house. Indeed, the layout of the «garden house» and the «public unit»  fits into the structure of contemporary society, transforming the courtyard house into a «miniature community.» The design of the apartments in minimal size serves the spiritual construction of the «garden house harmonization», and transforms the experience of everyday poetry and urban landscape into the «ideal living environment» through the narrative of space. This project also provides an extension of public space from the street and completes the established «street + residential unit» model, transforming the courtyard into a «miniature community». This collective space can be used and shared by all residents of the unit on a daily basis, and can be opened to neighbouring hutongs and foreign visitors. This space then becomes a place of public service shared by a larger number of neighbors and reinforces its «community» character.The interview is especially based on the analysis of the ‘Miniature Beijing’ project : a conversion of No. 28 Dayuan Hutong Beijing in collective housing, sharing spaces and facilities#China #contemporarychinesearchitecture #density #housing #architecture #cag #atelierli #lixinggang #architectureinterviews #architectinterviews #lifestyle #collectivehousing #minimalliving #insideoutside #massproduction #customedarchitecture #context #hutong #history

In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

I learned from @colleudumond (merci!) that the garden I shared yesterday at Chaumont-sur-Loire was designed by Wang Shu, a Chinese architect who has won the Pritzker prize. I looked up more of his work and was very interested in much of what I saw and read. Both in terms of how he and several other architects have been changing Chinese architecture in the last 20 or so years, but also in the specifics of how. Particularly interesting to me was Wang Shu’s Ningbo History Museum where he used materials salvaged from building and villages that had been cleared for the project in the facade. In his own words the design was a kind of resistance against the thoughtfulness destruction of their history. This was designed in 2008 around the same time as the Beijing Olympics, so I can only imagine how relevant that statement was.

Interesting to me is that I recognize a global trend that we also saw in Europe and elsewhere in the same period using salvaged and traditional materials in a way that honored but also transcends the vernacular.

The museum intentionally reminds us of both large ruins and fortresses and is an imposing figure in the landscape. The angles of the facade create tension and different scale spaces from very large to intimate, and paths seem to zigzag between. The contrast of the deeply textural and detailed facade to the enormous scale of the building adds so much. It is the materials that bring the whole building to life for me and make it most interesting.

Architect: Amateur Architecture Studio, Beijing Project team: Wang Shu, Lu Wenyu, Song Shuhua, Jiang Weihua, Chen Lichao Structural engineers: Shentu Tuanbing, Chen Yongbing Construction supervisor: Hu Jun Photographs: Iwan Baan

The original house is preserved, and does not destabilize the rest of the adjoining housing. The house is based on a modular architecture, this is possible by the use of prefabricated materials. This off -site production allows a quick realization once on site, which turns out to be very cheap.The house itself is completely adapted to its inhabitants and personalized to their uses. This is an essential notion in the development of DTP projects: the human being is at the heart. In the Huang house, on a poor area of 15m2, the kitchen and water space on the ground floor, followed by the bedroom on the first  floor. This minimal relationship to space projects the need for sharing and common spaces towards the outside and thus an appropriation of the street. For the Fang house, small front and back outdoor spaces are  created on the plot, the 25m2 house proposes a 1 bedroom housing on one level.

Shuifa Geographic Information Industrial Park Exhibition Center 
#Jinan, #China

The project is located in the Changqing Economic Development Zone, 20 kilometers away from the city centre of Jinan. In order to give visitors the best viewing experience, the designer has isolated the area from the surrounding environment and has created a relatively enclosed space.

The building’s main functions are hosting residential sales expos, property expos, and offices. The main entrance is located on the west side. In order to eliminate the visual impact of the messy surrounding environment, geometrical hills are designed to surround the square, which slowly rises as people enter the site, gradually blocking out the view. Mountains, water, and marble are fused together in this undeveloped wilderness.

A second layer is set outside the main structure - perforated plating, so that the building is enveloped within the perforated plating, forming a relatively enclosed space. The curtain wall sections are slanted, nestled, and interlaced inside, and the gap between the sections naturally forms the entrance of the building. Everything happens inside the space covered by the perforated plate curtain wall, connected to the outside world only through the irregular gaps. The interior of the building is obscured by the white perforated plating, and as night falls, light shines through the perforated plates to make the whole building glow, like a piece of shiny marble standing in the wilderness.

Architects: aoe @aoe.architect 
Area: 5200 m²
Year: 2020
Photographs: Vincent Wu

I learned from @colleudumond (merci!) that the garden I shared yesterday at Chaumont-sur-Loire was designed by Wang Shu, a Chinese architect who has won the Pritzker prize. I looked up more of his work and was very interested in much of what I saw and read. Both in terms of how he and several other architects have been changing Chinese architecture in the last 20 or so years, but also in the specifics of how. Particularly interesting to me was Wang Shu’s Ningbo History Museum where he used materials salvaged from building and villages that had been cleared for the project in the facade. In his own words the design was a kind of resistance against the thoughtfulness destruction of their history. This was designed in 2008 around the same time as the Beijing Olympics, so I can only imagine how relevant that statement was.

Interesting to me is that I recognize a global trend that we also saw in Europe and elsewhere in the same period using salvaged and traditional materials in a way that honored but also transcends the vernacular.

The museum intentionally reminds us of both large ruins and fortresses and is an imposing figure in the landscape. The angles of the facade create tension and different scale spaces from very large to intimate, and paths seem to zigzag between. The contrast of the deeply textural and detailed facade to the enormous scale of the building adds so much. It is the materials that bring the whole building to life for me and make it most interesting.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

Seeds are the main raw material used to make Chinese liquor. At the entrance lobby, various seeds are placed in Plexiglas tubes to create a vibrant screen with a huge pattern.

PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

I learned from @colleudumond (merci!) that the garden I shared yesterday at Chaumont-sur-Loire was designed by Wang Shu, a Chinese architect who has won the Pritzker prize. I looked up more of his work and was very interested in much of what I saw and read. Both in terms of how he and several other architects have been changing Chinese architecture in the last 20 or so years, but also in the specifics of how. Particularly interesting to me was Wang Shu’s Ningbo History Museum where he used materials salvaged from building and villages that had been cleared for the project in the facade. In his own words the design was a kind of resistance against the thoughtfulness destruction of their history. This was designed in 2008 around the same time as the Beijing Olympics, so I can only imagine how relevant that statement was.

Interesting to me is that I recognize a global trend that we also saw in Europe and elsewhere in the same period using salvaged and traditional materials in a way that honored but also transcends the vernacular.

The museum intentionally reminds us of both large ruins and fortresses and is an imposing figure in the landscape. The angles of the facade create tension and different scale spaces from very large to intimate, and paths seem to zigzag between. The contrast of the deeply textural and detailed facade to the enormous scale of the building adds so much. It is the materials that bring the whole building to life for me and make it most interesting.

Architect: Amateur Architecture Studio, Beijing Project team: Wang Shu, Lu Wenyu, Song Shuhua, Jiang Weihua, Chen Lichao Structural engineers: Shentu Tuanbing, Chen Yongbing Construction supervisor: Hu Jun Photographs: Iwan Baan

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project (with my partners of @zhijian_workshop) :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

"Jiu Qu", a brick shaped solid composite of yeast and mold, is used for saccharification and fermentation. We used these vegetal bricks to create the counter of the bar, which gives an olfactive experience to the user. The countertop is made of custom terrazzo fabricated on site with pieces of green glass from local bottles of liquor.

@ensa_versailles The density of other surrounding villages was studied to set Dongziguan’s one. They wanted to have modular typologies to combine them in different ways and create new areas in the village, to create unique space into a modern pattern of living. They set the buildings to create space between them, with differents uses for each of them. Through the collaborative sessions with the inhabitants, they were able to propose differents uses for the types of outdoor spaces: relaxing, nature connection or storage for instance. PRODUCTION*Density / Ecological Urbanism (Taillandier Paris)Curator : @ulysse_dhn @ensa_versailles It is within the framework of Wang Hao agency’s work in the category of «reshaping the value of places» that the project of the new Guiyuan village in Shaoxing city is included. Through this project he tries to transmit many key points of his vision of architecture. Firstly the question of sharing knowledge, showing the public what the architect can do for them. Secondly, the question of «reshaping the value of places». In a Chinese context in which architecture is not meant to last, thinking about the place of ruins and the possibility of renovating and rehabilitating them tends to be poetic. In a part of our discussion he defined this project as a landscape research, he worked this building as a landscape. Originally this unfinished building was used as a kindergarten for a while before being returned to its abandoned ruin status. In the rather particular context of Shaoxing, which he defined as the Chinese Venice, one can imagine that the place of water plays a key role in the landscape. Unfortunately, after the urbanization, many canals have been waterproofed to serve as roads. Through this project he seeks to sublimate the ruin while echoing the landscape of yesterday by integrating canals in roofs and basins in the ground floor. Within the framework of this project we find private spaces reserved for offices, meeting rooms but also many exhibition spaces that can be appropriated at different times by the inhabitants. (...)The interview is especially based on the analysis of the Guiyuan New Village Community Renovation Yuecheng in Zhejiang province 2018

For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

When entering the entrance lobby, visitor stands on a transparent carpet made of glass. Underneath lies a series of jars that are half buried, giving the illusion of ancient jars. This setting reminds of the courtyards of traditional distilleries, in which jars were placed on the floor, very close to each other, entirely covering the surface of the floor and forming a sort of carpet. This carpet extends to the outdoor space and becomes a water fountain. The sequences of circulation become obvious.

In the context of Brilliant city project study, we met professor Fan Lang that conducted her Phd on co-living and density upon Brilliant city case study: https://www.theses.fr/2018STRAG020中远两湾城 (zhongyuan liangwancheng), Brilliant City is an urban renewal project of a neighborhood in Shanghai. Originally slums located near the Suzhou River, at the end of the XXth century began a large renovation project. The project was developed by the architectural firm ECADI (East China Architectural Design & Research Institute) with Mr Shen Di as the Head Architect, and with the help of the international landscape firm, EDAW. The neighborhood is constituted of 96 skyscrapers with an average height of 90 meters. The FAR is approximately 5.7 (2million square meters of inhabitable space by 373 thousand square meters, the surface of the lot). The density is a big focal point in the project. It is located at the Heart of Shanghai, with a density of 3854 inhabitant/km2. Plus, it arrived at the time when there was a big shortage in housing in Shanghai. It suggested a new way of living, a new way of developing the city which responded to the challenges of the time, with a big emphasis on the quality of life in relationship to the living area.

Welcome to a special journey through the traditional making of Chinese liquor! A glimpse at our newly completed project :Chinese liquor themed boutique hotel.
...
For this renovation project, the client wanted the new design to focus on the topic of traditional Chinese liquor. In China, alcohol is made from cereal seeds, following a traditional liquor-making process that has been used over centuries. 

After a careful study of this process, we created a specific architectural scenography that gives people a singular sensory experience of the making of traditional Chinese liquor. 

When entering the entrance lobby, visitor stands on a transparent carpet made of glass. Underneath lies a series of jars that are half buried, giving the illusion of ancient jars. This setting reminds of the courtyards of traditional distilleries, in which jars were placed on the floor, very close to each other, entirely covering the surface of the floor and forming a sort of carpet. This carpet extends to the outdoor space and becomes a water fountain. The sequences of circulation become obvious.

I learned from @colleudumond (merci!) that the garden I shared yesterday at Chaumont-sur-Loire was designed by Wang Shu, a Chinese architect who has won the Pritzker prize. I looked up more of his work and was very interested in much of what I saw and read. Both in terms of how he and several other architects have been changing Chinese architecture in the last 20 or so years, but also in the specifics of how. Particularly interesting to me was Wang Shu’s Ningbo History Museum where he used materials salvaged from building and villages that had been cleared for the project in the facade. In his own words the design was a kind of resistance against the thoughtfulness destruction of their history. This was designed in 2008 around the same time as the Beijing Olympics, so I can only imagine how relevant that statement was.

Interesting to me is that I recognize a global trend that we also saw in Europe and elsewhere in the same period using salvaged and traditional materials in a way that honored but also transcends the vernacular.

The museum intentionally reminds us of both large ruins and fortresses and is an imposing figure in the landscape. The angles of the facade create tension and different scale spaces from very large to intimate, and paths seem to zigzag between. The contrast of the deeply textural and detailed facade to the enormous scale of the building adds so much. It is the materials that bring the whole building to life for me and make it most interesting.
